queries: WITH r AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS rentals FROM rental re JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = re.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), o AS (SELECT AVG(rentals) AS avg_rentals FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.rentals) AS avg_rentals_above_avg_ratings, AVG(r.rentals - o.avg_rentals) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM r CROSS JOIN o WHERE r.rentals > o.avg_rentals

responses.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS rentals FROM rental re JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = re.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), o AS (SELECT AVG(rentals) AS avg_rentals FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.rentals) AS avg_rentals_above_avg_ratings, AVG(r.rentals - o.avg_rentals) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM r CROSS JOIN o WHERE r.rentals > o.avg_rentals

assumptions.assumption: Rental count per rating is the number of rental rows joined through inventory to film (each rental counted once).
The 'average across ratings' is the unweighted mean of the per-rating rental counts (5 ratings), not the per-film or per-rental average.
'Above average' is strictly greater than the mean; the 'overall average' is the mean of per-rating counts and the excess is measured against it.

assumptions.assumption: Rental volume per rating is the count of rental rows joined through inventory to film; the 'overall average' is the unweighted mean of the per-rating rental counts across the 5 ratings.
'Above the average' means strictly greater than the mean of per-rating counts.

responses.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS rentals FROM rental re JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = re.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), o AS (SELECT AVG(rentals) AS avg_all FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.rentals) AS avg_rentals_above_average_ratings, AVG(r.rentals - o.avg_all) AS avg_excess_over_overall_average FROM r CROSS JOIN o WHERE r.rentals > o.avg_all

assumptions.assumption: 'How much each rating gets rented' is the number of rental rows per rating (rental -> inventory -> film), not distinct films or distinct customers.

The 'average across ratings' is the unweighted mean of the 5 per-rating rental counts. The ratings above it are kept, and the output is the mean of their counts plus the mean of their differences from that overall mean.
